headline: Incident time, production currency, and eventual recovery now form one honest, self-validating evidence lifecycle.

items.title: Incident onset became an evidence-bounded interval
items.insight: RUM, uptime, and route provenance retain their own roles and resolutions; unrelated promotion history is explicitly excluded.

items.title: Production shell parity now proves the deployed route
items.insight: One generic parser compares local route HTML with the same remote route and survives CI vantage challenges without erasing truth.

items.title: The first real recovery will close itself exactly once
items.insight: Synthetic tests enforce invariants, but only a committed real semantic transition can publish live recovery proof.

items.title: Local self-comparison cannot masquerade as production evidence again
items.insight: A structural gate rejects local production callers, missing canonical origins, and parser duplication.

items.title: Humans can see staging readiness and production currency separately
items.insight: The public status page exposes commit distance and shell drift without borrowing a green candidate state.

items.title: Daily RUM updates cannot strand downstream trust feeds
items.insight: The RUM publisher now rebuilds and stages Worker history, public status, status proof, and citation in one commit.

items.title: A transient package-name collision became a studio-wide guard proposal
items.insight: Bare npx names require exact package trust and bin identity before future execution.

followUps: Observe and validate the first real mismatch-to-matched recovery after legitimate production promotion.
blockers: Production promotion remains held on incomplete Supabase/identity/provider proof; production is stale and Worker routes remain 0/5 matched.
